subject.title: [Bug] Docker sandbox container name collision across multiple instances on same host

question: Should OpenClaw scope all non-shared sandbox runtime identities by resolved workspace and accept the documented one-time runtime reset, or require a preservation/migration path before fixing this collision?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but the durable fix changes sandbox identity and cleanup behavior across Docker, browser, SSH, registry, and skills workspace paths, which is a sandbox-boundary and upgrade decision.

options.title: Accept workspace-scoped non-shared identity
options.body: Land the current candidate direction after explicitly accepting that old non-shared runtimes are recreated under workspace-scoped identities and cleaned up by recreate or prune.

options.title: Require migration before merge
options.body: Ask for a doctor or migration path if preserving old non-shared runtime state matters more than one-time recreation.

options.title: Split backend policy
options.body: Pause the candidate fix if Docker, browser, SSH, and skills workspace identity should not move together under one scope-key contract.

recommendation.title: Accept workspace-scoped non-shared identity
recommendation.body: Land the current candidate direction after explicitly accepting that old non-shared runtimes are recreated under workspace-scoped identities and cleaned up by recreate or prune.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history and product-context signals point to steipete for sandbox security and lifecycle direction.
